hypothesis: Adding a steep hinge penalty only when the raw upper-tier area ratio leaves a narrow dead-band around 0.5 makes the raw partition land inside the official 47-53% band so the fixed balance-repair step flips far fewer nodes, preserving the learned cut structure and lowering TNS.
analysis: (1) No. All runs valid, but every circuit regressed (total −1.060, robust −0.510). (2) C1–C3 all worsened: cut nets rose (137→180, 318→383, 582→641), wcut rose, and crit_cross jumped sharply (0.011→0.104, 0.000→0.140, 0.069→0.171); repair_flips also increased (103→117, 238→244, 353→370), contradicting the predicted flip reduction. The hinge apparently pushed partitions away from 0.5 rather than into the dead-band, degrading cut structure and TNS. (3) Seed spread is high (std 0.261; C3 per-seed −0.05 to −0.84), not acceptable. (4) Instrument the raw area ratio distribution per seed to verify the hinge actually lands in 47–53%; if not, retune the dead-band/threshold before retesting.
